title: Frith & Fell - Cosy Colony Sim - New Play Test on Itch.io
author: JWalter89
selftext:
Hello everyone!

\>tl;dr - I've got a new playable build of my colony sim game on [itch.io](https://games-by-jon.itch.io/frith-and-fell) and I'd love for you to play it. And let me know what you think either through the ingame feedback, or on [Discord](https://discord.gg/DkMVRW7Ug6)

Since July I've been working on Frith & Fell, it's a cosy colony sim about a logging company in a valley. It's built in C# for the simulation, and then Godot on top of it.  

  

My entire workflow process has been using Opus or Fable as an orchestrator and offloading to other Claude agents to break the tasks down. I've used GitHub for source control and issue tracking - but eventually built a game dashboard so I can quickly go through and make comments or request new features, which has worked really well!

I also made use of Blender MCP, and Librescipt MCP to help me turn my shoddily made assets into more game ready assets.

The game started out initially from boredom one evening where I asked Claude to recommend me some games, and then it offered to help me design a game based on things I liked. And that game, turns out, is massively ambitious. So I suggested narrowing the scope into a number of smaller games that can coalesce into what that would be. And here we are!

The main idea behind the game is that you own a logging company in a generated valley, you start off with 3 workers. Each worker is an individual, they have their own wants, needs, strengths, weaknesses, and they're really a complete Player Character. If you want, at any point, you can take control of them (like in Dungeon Keeper) and wander through the forest, cutting down trees, and carrying logs.

Or you can play in the main architect view and order them around. You can take on commissions and contracts to earn money and rewards, or just sell what you make. You can hire more people and grow your company.

There's a (what I think anyway) solid gameplay loop of studying the forest, cutting down trees, processing the logs into planks, and then eventually furniture. Selling the output of that and then buying more land. 

One of the most useful things, I found, was to create a skill that lets Claude watch videos through yt-dlp, so if I was trying to articulate a concept I could send Claude a video to watch and we'd then discuss what I'm trying to achieve and go from there. Which was very helpful.

**I'm looking for people to play test the game and see what works, what doesn't, and what I could improve. And I'd really appreciate your feedback! Check it out on** [**itch.io**](https://games-by-jon.itch.io/frith-and-fell) **and send me feedback ingame or on** [**Discord**](https://discord.gg/DkMVRW7Ug6)

**Thanks for your time.**

comments.author: biggdogg420
comments.body: The handoff between architect mode and direct control is the first thing I’d test. Order one worker to deliver a log, take control halfway there, then release them after dropping it somewhere else. Does the worker resume, replan, or wait for you? A one-line reason beside their new task would make a good way to tell whether the sim understood the handoff.

replies.author: JWalter89
replies.body:
In short, it replans.

There's a worker brain and task ladder that runs through each character. When you possess a character mid-task the ladder is obviously no longer applied as you have agency over it. But when you then dispossessed a character the brain and ladder get re-applied. So the task is essentially forgotten, and then replans.

If a log has just been left on the floor, it counts as loose stock so a hauling task is created for it again.
